topic: The Birthing of Aiche’s Process Development Division
title: The Birthing of Aiche’s Process Development Division
session_title: Plenary: Historical Perspective of Process Development - PDD 25th Anniversary Celebration (Invited Talks)
abstract: The presenters will review the state or relevant programming within AIChE during the early 1990s and discuss the motivations for change and the steps leading to a new division. At that time only the skeleton of a former Engineering Division (Group 12) remained with no divisional leadership or structure. Its only functioning group was a programming entity called “Pilot Plants Committee “(Area 12a), that organized two sessions at both the Fall and Spring Meetings, This Pilot Plant Committee had a meeting at each conference, to plan programming for future sessions. At one of these meetings in New Orleans (1996), there was a discussion about expanding the scope of the programing to other topics of process engineering. With encouragement by AIChE staff a decision was finally made to propose a new division to replace the old Engineering Division. After considerable brainstorming this resulted in the adoption of the name, “Process Development Division”. Discussions both within the new entity and with AIChE leadership continued through several more conferences and led to the formation of a formal Steering Committee focused on the development of specific areas of programing to reside in the newly proposed division. In 1997-1998, the programming structure for the new division (which retained the AIChE programming committee designation of Group 12) was resolved. Four programming areas were developed: Areas; 12a "Process Research and Innovation" 12b "Pilot Plants",12c "Technology Transfer" and 12d"Manufacturing", along with their initial leadership. The Fall 1999 Dallas Meeting saw the debut of the finalized structure, leadership and programming required for the Process Development Group to apply to become a division of AIChE. The Process Development Division was formally approved in 2020 by AIChE after completion of all the formal requirements (including official bylaws).

topic: The Yoga, Pilates, and Cardio of Process Development
title: The Yoga, Pilates, and Cardio of Process Development
session_title: Plenary: Historical Perspective of Process Development - PDD 25th Anniversary Celebration (Invited Talks)
abstract: The origins and growth of the Process Development Division model the Best Practices seen in industry. We’ll review What we did right: how the Division’s history models the “best practice” process development workflow, and how consistency and discipline (as in a dedicated exercise regimen) contributed to its success. Our product quality: the Division’s “tree” within AIChE leadership and membership, and Our market projections: how the Division’s history can guide its continued growth and success

topic: A Ride on the PDD Time Machine – 20 Years
title: A Ride on the PDD Time Machine – 20 Years
session_title: Plenary: Historical Perspective of Process Development - PDD 25th Anniversary Celebration (Invited Talks)
abstract: The organizational structure of the fledging Process Development Division (PDD) was the focus of a Short Course during the 2005 AIChE Spring Meeting held in Atlanta. This presentation will take us back to a time when PDD had fully developed the four initial focus areas, Innovation & Research, Pilot Plant / Scale-up, Technology Transfer, and Manufacturing . Several select slides used for that short course will be presented to show the a.) what, b.) who, and c.) how each area functioned, concluding with an overview of how all areas were integrated into what the Process Development Division was 20 years ago. One may find that many of the elements presented remain germane in today’s PDD. About John Corn He specialized in Pilot Plant design/operations and Process Design. He held a part-time Instructor position at The Ohio State University in Columbus, OH. John had been active in Chemical Process Development and Plant Safety for over 30 years and was a charter member and past chair of the AIChE Process Development Division. He held a PE license in Ohio and was a certified Process Hazard Analysis Team Leader.
